description:
**Bug:** `Fetcher::PeriodicCleanup.restart_fiber` (src/fetcher/periodic_cleanup.cr) creates a new `stop` channel and overwrites `@@stop_channel`, but the *previous* cleanup fiber still holds its own closure-captured copy of the *old* `stop` channel. Replacing the global doesn't reach the old fiber, so the old fiber keeps running forever — doing cleanup work against stale rules, leaking one fiber per `force: true` restart.

```crystal
private def self.restart_fiber : Nil
  stop = Channel(Bool).new
  @@stop_channel = stop
  @@cleanup_running = true
  old_fiber = @@global_cleanup_fiber  # never used
  @@global_cleanup_fiber = spawn do
    loop do
      selected = select               # assignment is no-op
      when stop.receive               # still listening on the OLD stop
        break
      ...
```

The trailing comment `# (handled by replacing @@stop_channel with new channel above)` shows this was thought to work but doesn't.

**Fix:**
1. Track each fiber's own `stop` channel (e.g., a `Tuple(Fiber, Channel(Bool))` or pair them in instance variables/closures).
2. On restart, `old_stop.send(true)` or `old_stop.close` *before* spawning the new fiber so the old one exits cleanly.
3. Drop the `selected = select` no-op assignment.
4. Add a regression spec: start periodic cleanup with interval A, restart with force + interval B, verify only one fiber is alive (e.g., via `Fiber.list` or by counting cleanups triggered).

Acceptance: spec passes; `ameba Lint/UselessAssign` for `old_fiber` and `selected` in this file is gone.
title: Fix periodic_cleanup fiber leak on restart
